title: Plexus: Taming Billion-edge Graphs with 3D Parallel Full-graph GNN Training
problem: Graph neural networks (GNNs) on large real-world graphs with billions of edges exceed GPU memory capacity. Distributed full-graph training suffers from high communication overhead and load imbalance due to irregular graph structure. Mini-batch sampling approaches sacrifice model quality.
motivation: Large-scale graphs (social networks, knowledge bases, scientific graphs) require efficient distributed training. Current approaches trade off between scalability (sampling) and quality (full-graph). Need for scalable full-graph training on billion-edge graphs.
method: Three-dimensional (3D) parallel approach for full-graph GNN training combining spatial and temporal parallelism. Double permutation scheme for load balancing addresses irregular graph structure. Performance model predicts optimal 3D configuration automatically. Evaluated on six graph datasets across up to 2048 GPUs (Perlmutter) and 1024 GPUs (Frontier).
key_novelty: 3D parallelism combining spatial and temporal dimensions for full-graph GNN training; double permutation load balancing; automatic configuration optimization via performance model.
contributions: 3D parallel approach for full-graph GNN training
Double permutation scheme for load balancing on irregular graphs
Performance model for automatic 3D configuration optimization
Unprecedented speedups: 2.3-12.5x over SOTA on multiple platforms
limitations: Specific graph dataset characteristics not detailed
Comparison with mini-batch sampling quality trade-offs not discussed
Memory requirements and per-GPU footprint not specified
Applicability to dynamic or streaming graphs unclear
